$comment: kit-lint rule 8 (wave 6A): interactive elements that draw their own states instead of the quietControl() contract, each with the reason it is not a quiet control. An entry that matches nothing fails as stale.

allow.reason: A menu option: Bits moves data-highlighted with the pointer and the keyboard, so the listbox highlight (bg-foreground/10) is its hover and its focus at once (DESIGN.md, options in a listbox). A separate :hover fill would show two highlighted rows.
A menu option: Bits moves data-highlighted with the pointer and the keyboard, so the listbox highlight is its hover and its focus at once (DESIGN.md, options in a listbox).

The drawer backdrop is the scrim over the whole page below the md step: pressing anywhere outside the drawer closes it. It is not a control a pointer aims at, and a quiet fill across the viewport on hover would read as a flash, not a state.
A managed menu option: Base UI supplies data-highlighted for keyboard and pointer feedback through the same canonical menu recipe as the Svelte adapter.
A native link inside a managed menu option; the menu highlight owns pointer and keyboard feedback rather than a second hover row.
The mobile drawer backdrop is the viewport scrim, matching the Svelte adapter. Hovering the whole page must not paint a quiet-control fill.
